kak-prosmotret-analitiku:
On the “Analytics” tab, you can see your transport performance indicators at a glance. Here you can see overall statistics and detailed charts for various parameters.

Statistics are shown for the last 24 hours.

At the top of the screen there are information blocks with the main indicators, for example:

  • Idle time

  • Mileage

  • Number of vehicles

  • Working time

Below are charts that help you assess the situation visually, for example, “Vehicle status”, “Connection”, “Mileage”, “Violation control”, “Geofences”, etc.

The set of available charts depends on the modules you have connected. If you have the PTM module, “Violation control”, “Geofences” and other modules connected, the corresponding charts appear in analytics automatically.

How to configure analytics

You can choose which information blocks and charts you want to see:

1. Tap the settings button

2. In the “Transport info blocks” section, select the checkboxes for the indicators you need

3. In the “Charts” section, select the charts that matter to you

All charts you created in the web version (including through templates) are also available in the mobile app.

Configuring charts

Some charts have additional settings. For example, in the “Mileage” chart you can set a limit (for example, 100 km).

The chart will then show:

  • How many vehicles traveled less than 100 km

  • How many vehicles traveled more than 100 km

    You can set any limit you need to understand the statistics.
kak-rabotat-s-ii-podderzhkoj:
AI support helps you get to grips with PILOT: it suggests where to find the function you need and explains the sequence of steps. For example, you can ask the assistant how to build a report, set up an object, create a geofence or connect a device. Answers are generated automatically and may contain links to the documentation.

How to create a chat

1. Go to the “Menu” section

2. Open the “AI support” tab

3. Tap the plus icon in the upper right corner

4. In the “Ask a question” field, enter your question

5. Tap the send button

6. Wait for the assistant’s answer

If the answer is long, scroll the chat to read it in full. After the answer, you can ask a follow-up question in the same chat.

Chat history

All the chats you created are shown on the “AI support” tab. The chat name is based on the topic of the question or the creation date.

Tap a chat to return to the conversation, view a previous answer or continue the discussion. To start a conversation on a different topic, tap the plus icon and create a new chat.
kak-rabotat-s-geozonami-1:
When the “Geofences” module is connected to your account, you can work with geofences in the mobile app.

A geofence is an area on the map that you create to track object movement inside or outside it.

A “Geofences” tab appears in the “Menu” section. Here you can choose which zones to display on the map. Just select the checkboxes next to the geofences you need.

Go to the “Map” section, and you will see all the selected geofences on the map. You can track object movement within these zones.

The “Map settings” also let you turn geofence display on or off.

How to create a geofence

1. Tap “Add”

2. Specify the parameters:

  • Geofence name

  • The group it will belong to (or create a new group)

3. Set the geofence shape:

Circle — tap the map and drag to set the radius (you can change the radius by dragging the edge)

Polygon — mark points on the map one by one to set the boundaries

![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_geozonami_1_custom_8.png)   ![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_geozonami_1_custom_11.png)

4. Select the geofence color

If needed, tap “Clear” to undo your changes.

5. Tap “Save” — the geofence appears in the list
kak-rabotat-s-voditelyami-2:
When the “Drivers” module is connected to your account, you can work with driver information in the mobile app.

A “Drivers” tab appears in the “Menu” section. Tap it to see the list of all drivers in your account.

In the driver list, select the driver you need to open their card. The card shows the driver’s main information:

  • Driver’s name and photo (if uploaded)

  • The group the driver belongs to

  • Status or license number

  • E-mail address

  • Additional information

  • Driver’s contact number.

  • Vehicles the driver is assigned to

To find out which drivers are assigned to a specific object, go to the objects section. Tap the object menu to open additional actions for the object, and select the “Drivers” tab.

kak-rabotat-s-osmotrami:
When the “Service” module is connected to your account, you can work with inspections in the mobile app — a tool for checking the condition of vehicles.

With inspections you can:

— carry out inspections on vehicles

— record what was checked and the condition of the vehicle

— track the history of all inspections

An “Inspections” tab appears in the “Menu” section. Go to it, and you will see all completed inspections by object.

Use the “Search” field to find a specific inspection. You can also use the filters :

— by period — select the inspection dates

— by objects — select the objects that were inspected

— by inspections — select a specific inspection name

Tap the inspection you need in the list to open the completed inspection form with questions and answers. To view all questions and results, tap . To exit the inspection, tap “Exit inspection”.

How to carry out an inspection

  • Tap the button in the upper right corner of the screen

2. Select the vehicle you are going to inspect

To find a vehicle, use the “Search” field or the filters by vehicle model or year of manufacture.

3. Select the inspection type

Inspection forms with questions are created in the web version and can be filled in in the mobile app. To learn how to create an inspection form, read here.

4. Answer the questions

Answer all the questions in the inspection form. If necessary, attach photos to confirm the condition of the vehicle.

5. Add a signature

If a signature is required, sign in the designated field. If you didn’t manage to sign the first time, use the eraser to clear it and try again.

kak-prosmotret-video-1:
If the “Video” module is connected to your account and video devices are installed on your objects, you can view the video recorded by these devices.

Viewing the video stream

1. In the “Objects” section, select an object with a connected camera

2. Open the object menu and go to the “Video” tab

3. On this tab you will see previews of all connected cameras

4. Tap the camera you need to go to the video player

Playback controls

In the player you can:

Switch between cameras using the arrows

Turn camera sound on and off

Take screenshots

Expand the video to full screen

Viewing video history

  • To view video history, tap the icon in the upper right corner of the player

kak-rabotat-s-komandami:
With the mobile app, you can send commands to objects to control them remotely:

1. Go to the “Objects” section and select the object you want to send a command to

2. Tap the object menu and select the “Commands” tab

**![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_komandami_custom_2.png)**![](images/drex_kak_rabotat_s_komandami_custom_3.png)

3. On the “Commands” tab, you will see a list of commands that can be run for the selected object, for example, sending an SMS command to the device, requesting settings, etc.

Tap the command you need to send it to the device.

In the “Command history” block, you can see all previously sent commands, their statuses and details:

  • Command name

  • Status

  • Command type

  • User who sent the command

kak-poluchit-syrye-tochki:
Raw points are unprocessed data that the device sends directly to the system in real time. They show what values come from the sensors without filtering or processing.

How to view raw points

1. Open the object menu

2. Go to the “Points” tab

On this tab you will see the data that the device sends.

To view the full set of unprocessed data:

— tap “Raw data”

— if needed, you can copy the data by tapping the “Copy” button

Viewing points on a chart

To view the data on a chart:

1. Switch to chart mode

2. Select one or more parameters to display on the chart. To do this, turn on the switch next to the parameter you need

The chart shows the values of the selected parameters. If you hover over a specific point, a tooltip appears with the exact time and value at that moment.

Configuring the display of point fields

On the “Points” tab, you can configure how data is displayed:

— select which parameters to show for each GPS point

— filter the points you need by time range
kak-postavit-obekt-na-okhranu:
To arm an object, a security sensor must be set up on it. If the sensor is set up, an “Arming” item appears in the object menu.

For the function to work, command templates named arm and disarm must also be created in the system. Set them up in the web interface beforehand, and the arming commands will appear:

  • Arm — arm the object

  • Disarm — disarm the object

When the security status changes, the corresponding icon appears next to the object in the list:

— object is armed

— object is disarmed

How to set up command templates

Command templates are set up in the PILOT web interface:

1. Open the user account

2. Go to the “Main” section

3. Click the “Commands” icon

3. A window opens where you can create command templates.

How to create a command template

1. Click “Add command”

2. Select the object the command is created for

3. Click

3. Specify the parameters:

  • Command type — GRPS

  • Command kind — SMS_VIA_GPRS

4. In the “SMS” field, enter the command text, for example: setdigout 0 — disarm

5. If needed, select the hex checkbox if the command must be sent in HEX format

6. Click “Save as template” and enter a name

Template names must be exactly as follows:

  • arm — arm the object

  • disarm — disarm the object

    The names are written in lowercase. The app uses these names to find and run the commands.

Command examples

Arming — arm

  BLEOUTPUT 0

Disarming — disarm

telegram-bot: The Telegram bot lets you work with the vehicles in your account, get information about objects, see their locations and use your phone as a GPS tracker.
kak-podklyuchitsya-i-polzovatsya-chat-bo:
In this article you will learn:

— how to connect and log in to the chatbot

— how to use the menu and the main functions

— how to view the vehicle list

How to connect to the chatbot

1. Open Telegram and find the bot @skyelectronics_bot

2. Tap the “Start” button

3. Select “Start authorization”

4. Enter your account login and password

If you made a mistake, tap “Reset login” and start over.

How to use the bot menu

Tap the “Menu” button — the main functions appear:

Help

When you tap Help, you get a short welcome message from the bot.

In it, the bot explains what it can do:

— show the list of your vehicles

— give information on each vehicle

— provide your unique ID, which is needed for the tracker to work

Advanced Menu

When you tap this command, an extended menu with buttons appears:

  • Vehicles — shows the list of all your vehicles

  • Get ID — the bot sends you your unique ID

    The ID is the number of a virtual GPS tracker. It works like a real tracker in a vehicle, except that the data is transmitted through Telegram from your phone.

  • Get user — shows which account you are currently logged in to

  • Log out — you log out of the account in the bot

Change language

Use this button if you want to change the bot interface language.

Version bot

Shows the current version of the bot.

How to get the vehicle list

1. Make sure you are logged in to the bot

2. Go to Advanced Menu to open the extended menu

3. Select “Vehicles” — the list of vehicles in the account is displayed

If you select a specific vehicle, the bot shows:

— a summary for the object

— a map link to view the location

When working with the vehicle list, you can search for the vehicle you need by typing text. Just write in the chat, for example: “Show vehicles” “Find vehicle 7009”

The bot recognizes the digits and letters of the number and picks all matching options. If there are matches in the list, it shows only the vehicles that fit your query.

kak-sozdat-svoj-telegram-bot:
To create a Telegram bot yourself, you need the official @BotFather service — the main Telegram bot through which all other bots are created and configured.

2. Tap Start to open the menu

kak-peredavat-statusy-i-mediafajly-chere:
The Telegram bot lets employees send information to PILOT directly from a mobile device. An employee can select the current status and also send a photo or video from the work site.

For example, an employee can send the statuses “On the way”, “Arrived at the site” and “Started work” in sequence, and after finishing, select the status “Work completed” and attach a photo of the result. Sent media files can be found and viewed in the PILOT web interface.

Setting up Telegram statuses

Statuses are created separately for each PILOT account. In the Telegram bot, an employee sees only the options that the master added in the settings of the corresponding account.

Setup is done by a user with master rights:

1. Log in to the PILOT web interface

2. Open “Contract settings”

3. Go to the “Telegram statuses” tab

4. Click “+ Add”

5. Enter the status name

6. Click “OK”

The created status appears in the general list. The value in the “Order” column determines its position among the other statuses.

To delete a status, select it in the list and click “Delete”.

After the account is connected to the Telegram bot, the created statuses become available to authorized users.

How to send a status

Logging in to the Telegram bot

Before starting, an employee needs to link the Telegram bot to a PILOT account:

1. Open the PILOT Telegram bot

2. Start the bot with the /start command

3. Enter the PILOT account login

4. Enter the password

5. Wait for the message confirming successful authorization

To log in, use the account in whose settings the master created the required statuses.

How to send a status in the bot

1. In the bot menu, tap “Status”

3. Select the status you need from the list provided

4. Wait for the “Status sent” message

The bot has accepted the selected status. After that, you can continue working with the bot: select another status when the work stage changes, or send a photo or video.

How to send a photo or video

Through the Telegram bot you can send materials that confirm completed work or show the condition of an object. For example, the work location, equipment before servicing, the result of the work, delivered cargo.

To send a file:

1. Open the PILOT Telegram bot

2. Tap the paperclip icon

3. Select a photo or video on your mobile device

4. Send the file

5. Wait for the “Media saved” message

The message confirms that the file has been received and saved in PILOT

How to view sent media files

The first time a media file is sent, a separate object named after the Telegram user is created in the PILOT object list. All subsequent photos and videos from this user are saved in the same object.

1. Open the “Online” tab in the PILOT web interface

2. Find the object named after the Telegram user in the tree

3. Right-click the object

4. Select “Media”

5. Specify the period for which to show materials

6. Find the record you need

7. Click the photo icon or the video icon to open the file

To save the file to your computer, click the download icon next to the corresponding record.

The “Media” tab shows the photos and videos sent by this user through the Telegram bot, as well as the date and time they were received.
pilot-driver:
PILOT Driver is a mobile app for drivers, couriers and delivery staff. It works together with PILOT Task Manager (PTM) and helps manage tasks and routes.

Tasks for drivers are created in the PTM web version and then passed to the PILOT. Driver mobile version, where drivers can view and carry them out.

With PILOT. Driver, drivers can carry out various types of tasks, for example:

  • Cargo delivery — tasks for delivering goods, materials or construction materials, for example, delivering goods, collecting and removing waste or delivering concrete

  • Taxi and tourism — for taxi drivers and drivers who work with tourists, PTM lets you manage transport orders

  • Waste collection — drivers can work on waste collection routes, marking each route point as they complete the task

How PTM works:

1. The driver receives a task with the route points to visit

2. While carrying out the task, the driver marks each route point as completed, confirming delivery or another job

3. After all route points have been visited, the driver marks the task as completed and, if necessary, sends a report on its completion

novye-zadaniya:
The “New” tab shows tasks that have been assigned to you and are waiting to be accepted. Until you tap the “Accept task” button, the task stays on this tab.

Each task is shown as a card with the main information:

— task name

— task number

— planned start date and time

— planned end date and time

— estimated duration

To open a task, tap its card.

Sorting tasks

If the list contains many tasks, you can change the order in which they are displayed.

To do this:

1. Open the “New” tab

2. Tap the list settings icon in the upper right corner

3. In the “List settings” window, select a sorting option:

  • Newest first — later tasks are shown at the top of the list

  • Oldest first — earlier tasks are shown at the top of the list

    4. Tap “Apply”

The list is updated automatically according to the selected sorting.

Viewing a task

To open a task, tap its card in the list.

After it opens, the task card with information is displayed.

The top of the card shows:

— start date and time

— end date and time

Below is the “Accept task” button, which puts the task in progress.

Task information

The “Task information” section shows the main details of the trip. The set of fields depends on the task type, but usually includes:

  • task name

  • customer or counterparty details

  • information about the vehicle, cargo, etc.

Waybill

Below is the “Waybill” section, which shows the route with all the visit points.

For each point, the following are shown:

  • address

  • point number

To see detailed information about a point, tap it in the waybill.

The window that opens shows:

— full address

— current point status

— “Actions” button

The “Actions” button gives access to the following functions:

  • Copy address — copy the address to the clipboard to use in a navigator or message

  • Show on map — open the map showing the location of the selected point

To open the route map, tap the map icon in the upper right corner of the task card. For more on working with the map, see the article “Route map”.
kak-prinyat-novoe-zadanie:
When a new task is assigned to you, it appears on the “New” tab.

To accept a task:

1. In the bottom menu, open the “New” tab

2. Find the task you need in the list and tap its card

3. Review the task information: start and end times, route, point addresses and other details.

4. If you are ready to start the task, tap the “Accept task” button.

After you accept it, the task automatically moves to the “Active” tab, where you can track its progress and work with route points.
aktivnye-zadaniya:
The “Active” tab shows tasks that you have already accepted and are currently carrying out. Here you can track progress, work with route points and complete tasks.

Each task is shown as a card with the main information:

— task name and number

— progress — the number of points completed out of the total

— planned start and end time

— a progress indicator showing how much of the route has been completed

Sorting tasks

If the list contains many tasks, you can change the order in which they are displayed.

To do this:

1. Open the “Active” tab

2. Tap the list settings icon in the upper right corner

3. In the “List settings” window, select a sorting option:

  • Newest first — newer tasks are shown first

  • Oldest first — earlier tasks are shown first

    4. Tap “Apply”

The list is updated automatically according to the selected sorting.

Viewing a task

To open a task, tap its card.

The task card shows:

— planned start and end time

— task type

— additional information (contact details, cargo information and other data)

— the route with the list of visit points

If the task has been accepted, tap the “Start task” button to begin carrying it out.

Working with route points

After you start the task, the screen shows the “Next point” block — the address to visit next.

The following actions are available for the selected point:

  • Route — build a route in the navigation app installed on the device

  • Arrived — mark your arrival at the point

After you tap “Arrived”, the point becomes active.

Additional actions become available for it:

— add a comment

— complete the point

— open the “Other actions” menu

You can use a comment to record additional information about the work performed, delivery or other events.

Other actions

Additional operations are available for the current point:

  • Copy address — copy the address to the clipboard

  • Show on map — open the point location on the map

  • Postpone point — temporarily defer the point

The postpone function can be useful in the following cases:

— the recipient is temporarily absent

— the point cannot be completed for external reasons

— you need to visit another route point first

After a point is postponed, it gets the “Postponed” status, and the app offers to move to the next route point. You can return to the postponed point later.

Progress

The current task progress is shown:

— in the active task list

— in the task card, in the “Progress” section

Task menu

In the upper right corner of the task card there is a menu button.

It gives access to the following actions:

  • Complete task — finish the task

  • Show full route — open the map with all route points

For more on working with the map, see the article “Route map”.

Completing a task

After you have performed all the required work and visited the route points, tap “Complete task”.

After completion, the task automatically moves to the “Completed” tab, where you can view it.
kak-zapolnit-otchyet:
If a report is set up for a task or route point, a “Fill in report” button appears in the app.

A report can be linked to:

— an individual route point

— the whole task

This depends on the settings specified by the operator in the web version of the system.

The composition and number of fields in a report may vary. What data must be filled in is determined by the report form settings.

How to open a report

1. Open an active task

2. If the report is linked to a route point, go to the point you need and tap “Arrived”

3. Tap the “Fill in report” button

The report form then opens.

Fields marked with the (*) symbol are required. Until the required fields are filled in, you cannot complete the report.

Filling in a report

Depending on the form settings, a report may contain various types of fields, for example:

  • text fields

  • numeric values

  • selection lists

  • switches

  • comment and signature fields

  • photos and files

Fill in all the required data according to your organization’s requirements.

Adding photos

If the form provides for photo capture, tap “Add photo”.

![](images/drex_kak_zapolnit_otchyet__custom_3.png)    ![](images/drex_kak_zapolnit_otchyet__custom_4.png)

In the window that opens, select one of the options:

  • Go to camera — take a photo with the device camera;

  • Choose photo from gallery — attach an existing image.

You can add several photos if needed.

How to complete a report

1. Make sure all required fields are filled in

2. Check that the data you entered and the attachments you added are correct

3. Tap the “Complete” button at the bottom of the screen

After successful completion, the report is saved and sent to the system.
zavershyennye-zadaniya:
The “Completed” tab shows all tasks that have been finished. Here you can view previously completed tasks and information about them.

Each task is shown as a card with the following information:

— task name

— task number

— start date and time

— end date and time

— actual completion time of the task

Sorting tasks

To change the order in which completed tasks are displayed:

1. Open the “Completed” tab

2. Tap the list settings icon in the upper right corner

3. In the “List settings” window, select a sorting method:

  • Newest first — recently completed tasks are shown at the top of the list

  • Oldest first — tasks completed earlier are shown at the top of the list

    4. Tap “Apply”

The list is then updated automatically.

Viewing a completed task

To open the information, tap the card of the task you need in the list.

The task card opens with information about the route, visited points and results.

Task information

The top of the card shows:

— start date and time

— end date and time

Below is the “Task information” section. Depending on the system settings, it may contain:

— task name

— company or customer name

— contact phone number

— office address

— task description

— cargo information

— other additional data

Waybill

The “Waybill” section shows all route points that were part of the task.

For each point, the following are shown:

— name and address

— point number

— completion status

— visit date and time

To view information about a point, tap it in the list.

The window that opens shows:

PILOT Tracker is an app that turns your smartphone into a GPS tracker. With it, you can track the device location in real time and send data to the server.

How to configure tracker parameters

The following settings are available on the app’s main screen:

Service status

• If the switch is on — the tracker is active and location data is being sent

• If the switch is off — the service is stopped and no data is sent

Device ID

The unique device number (for example, 705943). You need to give this number to technical support so that your device appears in the system.

Server URL

The address of the server that data is sent to. You can change this address if necessary.

Location accuracy

The higher the accuracy, the more precise the track, but it requires more power and traffic. Choose the best setting for your use.

Frequency

Set how often the tracker sends data to the server (for example, every 5 or 10 seconds). A shorter interval means a more detailed track but uses more battery and data.

Distance

Specify the distance traveled after which new points are sent. For example, every 50 m. This lets you avoid sending data when the object is barely moving.

Angle

Select the angle at which a new point is sent (for example, if the turn angle is greater than the set value).

Offline buffering

If you turn this option on, the tracker saves location data when there is no internet connection. As soon as the connection is restored, all accumulated data is automatically sent to the server.

Wake lock

If turned on, the app keeps the tracker running in the background, even if the phone is not in use.

“Status” tab

The “Status” tab shows the tracker’s operation log — here you can see the current state of the service as well as information about its recent operation.

At the top of the screen there is a “Clear” button, which deletes the current list of messages.

1. Open the “Information” tab in the app

This article shows an example of connecting through Microsoft Power BI. You can connect in the same way to any BI system that supports working with REST API.

How to add a query in Power BI

1. Open Power BI Desktop

Launch Power BI Desktop on your computer. If it is not installed, download it free of charge from the official Microsoft website.

2. On the main ribbon at the top, click the “Get data” button. A list of available data sources opens

3. From the list of data sources, select “Blank query”

4. The Power Query Editor opens — a window where data queries are created and configured.

In this window, find the “Advanced Editor” button on the toolbar at the top and click it.

5. The “Advanced Editor” window opens with an empty query template

6. Paste the query code (see the query example below)

In the query you need to specify:

  • Server address

  • Login — your login from the partner account

  • Password — your password from the partner account

  • Dates — the start and end date of the period

  • List of metrics — which data you want to get (see the full list of metrics below)

7. After pasting the code, click “Done”. Power BI starts connecting to the server and loading data

8. After that, Power BI may show the warning “Information is required about data privacy”. Click “Continue”.

9. The “Privacy Levels” window opens

In it, Power BI checks whether it is safe to combine and process data from the sources used in the query. In our case, the query accesses one trusted data source, and authorization is already performed inside the query itself. So that Power BI does not block loading or interfere with the query, select the “Skip privacy level checks for this file” checkbox.

Then click “Save”.

10. After you save, Power BI runs the query and opens a data preview in the Power Query Editor. A table with columns and rows appears on the screen — this is the data returned by your query.

11. Click “Close & Apply”. The data is then loaded into Power BI, and you can work with it.

You can now use the loaded data to create charts, tables and other visual elements.

The following panes are usually displayed on the right of the main Power BI Desktop window:

  • Visualizations — this is where the types of charts, diagrams, cards, tables and other visual elements are located. Select the type you need, then fill it with your fields

  • Data — this shows the list of tables and fields loaded from your query, for example, date, object ID, mileage, fuel consumption, average speed. Use these fields in visualizations: select them with checkboxes, drag them with the mouse or swap them

  • Filters — here you can limit the data by the conditions you need

How to build a chart

1. In the “Visualizations” pane, click the chart type you need. An empty chart template appears on the report canvas

2. In the “Data” pane, select the fields you want to show

3. Power BI automatically places the fields in the chart

In Power BI you can combine data:

  • add the same field to different charts

  • compare several indicators

  • build several visualizations on one page

  • replace fields without recreating the report

If the query does not refresh or login errors occur

Sometimes Power BI may keep the previous connection parameters for the data source. Because of this, even after you change the login, password or server address, the query may keep returning an authorization error. In this case, clear the saved permissions for the data source.

How to clear permissions:

1. In the Power Query Editor, click “Data source settings” on the toolbar

2. In the window that opens, select the data source you need, for example, your server address

1 — “Data source settings” button

2 — Selecting the data source

3 — “Clear Permissions” button

3. Click “Clear Permissions”

4. In the confirmation window, click “Delete”

5. Run the query again. Power BI then applies the connection parameters anew

This article provides example requests for working with the BI Analytics API. You can use them as a basis for connecting Power BI or another BI system that supports REST API.

Depending on your task, you can choose one of two options:

  • Basic example — suitable for getting to know the API, testing the connection and building simple integrations. It shows the minimum set of steps needed to authorize, send a request and receive data.

  • Advanced example — recommended for production integrations and regular data refresh. In addition to authorization and data retrieval, it includes API error handling, response structure validation, handling of empty results and automatic conversion of data into a format convenient for Power BI.

We recommend using the advanced example in production projects, as it provides more reliable error handling and makes the integration easier to maintain.

Basic request example

let
    BaseUrl = "https://<server_address>",
 
    LoginJson =
        Json.Document(
            Web.Contents(
                BaseUrl,
                [
                    RelativePath = "api/bi/login.php",
                    Headers = [#"Content-Type" = "application/json"],
                    Content = Json.FromValue([
                        username = "YOUR_LOGIN",
                        password = "YOUR_PASSWORD"
                    ]),
                    ManualStatusHandling = {400, 401, 403, 404, 500}
                ]
            )
        ),
 
    Token = LoginJson[access_token],
    NodeId = LoginJson[user][node_id],
 
    AnalyticsJson =
        Json.Document(
            Web.Contents(
                BaseUrl,
                [
                    RelativePath = "api/bi/analytics.php",
                    Query = [node = Text.From(NodeId)],
                    Headers = [
                        #"Authorization" = "Bearer " & Token,
                        #"Content-Type" = "application/json"
                    ],

Advanced request example

This example includes API error handling, response structure validation and automatic conversion of data into a Power BI table.

let
    BaseUrl = "https://pilot-gps.com",
 
    // --- API ERROR HANDLING ---
    ApiJson =
        (Response as binary, Context as text) as record =>
            let
                Status =
                    try Value.Metadata(Response)[Response.Status]
                    otherwise 200,
 
                ParsedJson =
                    try Json.Document(Response)
                    otherwise
                        error Error.Record(
                            Context,
                            "API response is not valid JSON",
                            [
                                status = Status,
                                body = Text.FromBinary(Response)
                            ]
                        ),
 
                ErrorMessage =
                    if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "error_description") then
                        ParsedJson[error_description]
                    else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "msg") then
                        ParsedJson[msg]
                    else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "errors") then
                        Text.Combine(List.Transform(ParsedJson[errors], each Text.From(_)), "; ")
                    else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "error") then
                        Text.From(ParsedJson[error])
                    else
                        "API request failed",
 
                CheckedJson =
                    if Status >= 400 then
                        error Error.Record(
                            Context,
                            ErrorMessage,
                            ParsedJson
                        )
                    else if Record.HasFields(ParsedJson, "success")
                        and ParsedJson[success] = false then
                        error Error.Record(
                            Context,
                            ErrorMessage,
                            ParsedJson
                        )
                    else
                        ParsedJson
            in
                CheckedJson,
 
    // --- LOGIN ---
    LoginResponse =
        Web.Contents(
            BaseUrl,
            [
                RelativePath = "api/bi/login.php",
                Headers = [#"Content-Type" = "application/json"],
                Content = Json.FromValue([
                    username = "LOGIN",
                    password = "PASSWORD"
                ]),
                ManualStatusHandling = {400, 422, 429, 500}
            ]
        ),
 
    LoginJson = ApiJson(LoginResponse, "BI Analytics login"),
 
    Token = LoginJson[access_token],
    NodeId = LoginJson[user][node_id],
 
    NodeQuery =
        if NodeId = null then
            []
        else
            [node = Text.From(NodeId)],
 
    // --- ANALYTICS REQUEST ---
    AnalyticsResponse =
        Web.Contents(
            BaseUrl,
            [
                RelativePath = "api/bi/analytics.php",
                Query = NodeQuery,
                Headers = [
                    #"Authorization" = "Bearer " & Token,
                    #"Content-Type" = "application/json"
                ],
                Content = Json.FromValue([
                    date_from = "2026-01-01",
                    date_to = "2026-12-31",
                    metrics = {
                        "veh_driving_dist",
                        "veh_fuel_cons",
                        "average_speed",
                        "veh_cars_counter"
                    },
                    source = "vehicle",
                    group_by = "source_day",
                    format = "flat",
                    page = 1,
                    per_page = 100
                ]),
                ManualStatusHandling = {400, 422, 429, 500},
                ExcludedFromCacheKey = {"Authorization"}
            ]
        ),
 
    AnalyticsJson =
        ApiJson(
            AnalyticsResponse,
            "BI Analytics request"
        ),
 
    // --- DATA CHECK ---
    DataList =
        if Record.HasFields(AnalyticsJson, "data") then
            AnalyticsJson[data]
        else
            error Error.Record(
                "BI Analytics response",
                "Response does not contain data field",
                AnalyticsJson
            ),
 
    // --- CONVERSION TO TABLE ---
    Tbl =
        if List.IsEmpty(DataList) then
            #table(
                {
                    "source_id",
                    "date",
                    "veh_driving_dist",
                    "veh_fuel_cons",
                    "average_speed",
                    "veh_cars_counter"
                },
                {}
            )

            Table.FromList(
                DataList,
                Splitter.SplitByNothing(),
                {"Column1"}
            ),
 
    Expanded =

            Table.ExpandRecordColumn(
                Tbl,
                "Column1",
                {
                    "source_id",
                    "date",
                    "veh_driving_dist",
                    "veh_fuel_cons",
                    "average_speed",
                    "veh_cars_counter"
                }

When sending requests to the BI Analytics API, you must specify parameters that define which data to retrieve and in what form to return it.

In addition to the request parameters, you must select metrics — the indicators that will be included in the result. They determine what data the API returns, for example mileage, fuel consumption, number of trips or eco-driving violations.

Main request parameters

Request parameters define the data source, the way the data is grouped and additional selection conditions.

source

The source field defines which data the selection is built from.

Available values:

  • vehicle — vehicle data

  • driver — driver data

group_by

The group_by field defines how to group the result.

  Value

  total
  Total for all vehicles or drivers for the period

  day
  Total for all vehicles or drivers for each day
  { "20260301": { "metric": 123 } }
  rating
  Each source, total for the period
  { source_id: { "metric": 123 } }
  source_day
  Each source, each day
  { source_id: { "20260301": { "metric": 123 } } }

ACCOUNT_ID

The ACCOUNT_ID parameter lets you limit the export to the data of a single contract.

If the request specifies the login and password of a partner account, then without ACCOUNT_ID the system exports all vehicles under all contracts available to this partner.

If you specify ACCOUNT_ID in the request, only the objects of the selected contract will be loaded.

rabota-s-api-zaprosami:
An API (Application Programming Interface) is a set of rules and tools that lets programs interact with each other. In PILOT, the API is used to exchange data between systems, services, applications and the platform.

An API request consists of:

  • URL — the API server address and the command

  • Request parameters — the data sent to the server

  • Request method — the way of interacting with the server

    How the API works in PILOT

PILOT uses a distributed infrastructure that includes several servers, for example, BLADE, KSA, AFRICA, USA. Each server can have several nodes, each with its own number.

When you send an API request to the system, specify the particular server (for example, BLADE) and the particular node within that server — node. This way, the request is processed directly on the selected server and node, without extra forwarding and with minimal response time.

Example request

https://blade.pilot-gps.com/api/api.php?cmd=list&node=14 

blade.pilot-gps.com is the server name

node=14 indicates the node (server) where the request must be processed.

To learn more about how to authorize and send requests to the PILOT server, read the next article.

Request methods in the API

GET

A method for getting data. It is used, for example, to request the list of objects or account information.

In a GET request, the command and parameters are passed directly in the URL. Parameters are added after the ? sign and separated by the & character.

Example

https://<server_address>/api/api.php?cmd=bindControl&uid=123&imei=456&lineuid=789

cmd=bindControl — command

uid=123, imei=456, lineuid=789 — parameters

POST

A method for sending data. It is used, for example, to create a new object or generate a report.

In a POST request, the command and parameters can be passed in the request body, or the command is specified in the URL and the parameters are passed in the body.

Example 1

URL: https://<server_address>/api/api.php?cmd=bindControl

Request body

 {
    "uid": "123",
    "imei": "456",
    "lineuid": "789"
  }

Example 2

URL: https://<server_address>/api/api.php

Request body

{
    "cmd": "bindControl",
    "uid": "123",
    "imei": "456",
    "lineuid": "789"
  }

PUT

A method for updating data. This type of request is used, for example, to change the parameters of an object or account.

PUT is most often used to update a specific resource, so the identifier is usually specified in the URL and the data to update in the body.

Example

URL: https://<server_address>/api/api.php/123

 Request body:

{
  "cmd": "updateControl",
  "uid": "123",
  "imei": "456",
  "lineuid": "789",
  "status": "active"
}

DELETE

A method for deleting data. For example, this method is used to delete an object or an account.

In a DELETE request, the command and parameters are usually passed in the URL.

Example

https://<server_address>/api/api.php?cmd=bindControl&uid=123&imei=456&lineuid=789

Data format

The API supports various formats for both requests and responses.

JSON:

{
  "cmd": "bindControl",
  "uid": "123",
  "imei": "456",
  "lineuid": "789"
}

Form-encoded:

cmd=bindControl&uid=123&imei=456&lineuid=789

XML:

<request>
  <cmd>bindControl</cmd>
  <uid>123</uid>
  <imei>456</imei>
  <lineuid>789</lineuid>
</request>

Data types

The API uses various data types to transfer information between the client and the server. Let's look at the main data types you may encounter in API requests and responses.

  Data type
  Description
  Example in JSON format
  What they are used for
  String
  Text in quotes
 "name": "Маршрут №9"
  For text data: names, descriptions,
  identifiers
  Number
Numeric value, integer or fractional
  "price": 15.35
  For numeric data: prices,
  identifiers, coordinates, time
  Array
  Ordered list of elements of any type
"points": [{"lat": "53.352142", "lon": "83.758749"},  {"lat": "52.534012", "lon": "85.178777"}]
  For lists of data: stops, goods,
  users

kak-podklyuchitsya-k-api:
This article explains how to authorize and send a request to the API. After that you will be able to send commands to the server and receive data from it.

API address

All requests are sent to the following address:

https://<server_address>/api/api.php

<server_address> is the address of the server or host where PILOT runs.

For example:

  • For users: https://pilot-gps.com/api/api.php

  • For administrators: https://admin.pilot-gps.com/ax/api.php

The API can be located in different “folders” of the project, and this is reflected in the request address, for example:

https://<server_address>/backend/api.php
https://<server_address>/ax/api.php

Folders (api, backend, ax and others) are simply the project structure. They show which set of commands you are accessing. Always use the full folder path given in the specific API command, otherwise the request will not work.

Authorization type

Basic Auth is used to connect to the API.

For the regular (user) API, sign in with the login and password of your account.

To work with the administrator API, use the administrator's login and password.

What a request looks like

The general form of a request is:

https://<server_address>/api/api.php?cmd=<command>&node=<node_num>

  • cmd — the command you want to execute

  • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed

Example response

In reply to your request, the server returns a response in JSON format:

{
  "code": 0,
  "msg": "OK",
  ...requested data...
}

  • code = 0 — everything completed successfully

  • code = 1 — an error occurred

  • msg — a message from the server (for example, "OK" or an error description)

If you prefer to work with XML, add the parameter out=xml to the request, and the result will come in XML format.

Example request:

https://<address>/api/api.php?cmd=<command>&node=<node_num>&out=xml

The response in this case will be:

<response>
  <code>0</code>
  <msg>OK</msg>
  ...requested data...
</response>

If you are just getting started with the API, we recommend first reading the article “Working with API requests” to understand what commands, parameters and data formats are.

This article describes the main API commands that let you interact with Linux systems through the Admin panel. With these commands you can send, receive, delete and view the history of commands for Atoms.

How to get the data

Request address

To get the data, use the address: https://<server_address>/backend/api.php

List of commands

  • cmd=atom_get_all — get the list of sent commands

  • cmd=atom_get_commands — get the list of command templates

  • cmd=atom_create_command — send a Linux command

  • atom_delete_command — delete a Linux command

Getting the list of sent Linux commands (command history)

This command lets you get the list of all commands sent to an Atom. The history includes the Atom identifier, the command sent, and the execution status.

Method: GET

Request parameters

  • cmd=atom_get_all — command to get the history

  • ident — unique Atom identifier (for example, b0:44:6t:0d:a9:04)

  • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed

    Example request

    https://<server_address>/backend/api.php?cmd=atom_get_all&ident=b0:44:6t:0d:a9:04&node=1

    Response

    [
      {
        "id": 27899,
        "agent_id": null,
        "ident": "8v:f5:8c:01:13:70",
        "script": "ls /root/",
        "processed": null,
        "ts": 1712138610,
        "result": null
      }
    ]

Getting the list of Linux command templates

This command lets you get the list of Linux command templates that can be used to send to an Atom. Templates contain a description and the command that will be executed on the device.

Method: GET

Request parameters

  • cmd=atom_get_commands — command to get command templates.

  • ident — unique Atom identifier (for example, 80:c5:80:01:68:08).

  • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed

    Example request

    https://<server_address>/backend/api.php?cmd=atom_get_commands&ident=80:c5:80:01:68:08&node=1

    Response

    [
      {
        "id": 36,
        "command_name": "Список Видео",
        "description": null,
        "command": "ls -lsh /video/*.avi"
      }
    ]

Sending a Linux command

With this command you can send a Linux command to an Atom. The command is added to the queue and executed on the device.

Method: POST

Request parameters

  • cmd=atom_create_command — command to create a new command.

  • ident — unique Atom identifier.

  • script — command script (optional).

  • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed

    Example request

    https://<server_address>/backend/api.php?cmd=atom_create_command&ident=b1:42:67:00:00:fd&node=1

    Response

27917 (ID of the command added to the queue)

Deleting a Linux command

If a command has not been executed yet, you can remove it from the queue using this method. Deletion is only possible before the command is processed.

Method: GET

Request parameters

  • cmd=atom_delete_command — command to delete

  • ident — unique Atom identifier

  • command_id — identifier of the command to delete

  • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed

    Example request

    https://<server_address>/backend/api.php?cmd=atom_delete_command&ident=b0:44:6f:0d:av:88&command_id=27921

    Response

    "Success delete"

API error codes

  • 400 Bad request — invalid data format or a required parameter is missing.

    Possible messages:

  • {"error": "Missing ident param"} — the Atom identifier is missing.

  • {"error": "Command already processed"} — the command has already been executed.

  • {"error": "Unknown macro: {Unknown macro}"} — unknown macro command.

  • 500 Internal server error — internal server error

Working with commands in the interface

In the PILOT interface, interaction with Atoms takes place through the “Auto Conductor → Buses” tab of the Admin panel, where the “Interact” command is available.

Through this function:

  • Commands (Linux commands) are sent to the Atom

  • You can view the list of available commands (templates)

  • The history of all sent commands is displayed

  • The result of each command's execution is available

This API loads the detailed points of the route (track) for a trip previously obtained via the rungeo method. Each track point contains coordinates, speed and the absolute registration time of the point in Unix timestamp format.

How to get the data

Method

GET

Request address

To get the data, use the address: https://<server_address>/api/api.php?

Request parameters

  • cmd = gettrack — command to get the track.

  • id — track identifier obtained in the response of the rungeo API

  • node — the number of the node on which the command must be executed

Example request

https://<server_address>/api/api.php?cmd=gettrack&id=70685695&node=1

Response

{
  "track_data": "47.2037;39.6325;10;1439443509:47.2037;39.6324;13;1439443510:47.2037;39.6323;15;1439443512:47.2036;39.6304;22;1439443568",
  "track_id": 70685695,
  "unixstarttimestamp": 1439443509
}

The API request returns:

  • track_id— unique track identifier;

  • unixstarttimestamp— date and time of the track start in Unix timestamp format;

  • track_data— sequence of track points separated by a colon (:).

Each track point consists of four values separated by a semicolon (;):

1. latitude — latitude;

2. longitude — longitude;

3. speed_kmh — speed in km/h;

4. point_unix_timestamp — absolute registration time of the point in Unix timestamp format, UTC.

Point format:

latitude;longitude;speed_kmh;point_unix_timestamp

Example:

47.2037;39.6325;10;1439443509

The value 1439443509 is the absolute registration time of the point, not the number of seconds from the start of the track.

To calculate the time elapsed since the start of the track, use the formula: elapsed_seconds = point_unix_timestamp - unixstarttimestamp. For example: 1439443568 - 1439443509 = 59

Deletes one or more notifications.

Request parameters:

  • id (optional) — ID of a specific notification

  • agent_id (optional) — if passed, all notifications for the specified agent are deleted

Example request

You can also delete all notifications by agent_id:

https://<address>/api/ptm/notification.php?agent_id=456

}

Request method

This API returns data on the operation of vehicle sensors for the selected period.

With it, you can:

— track the periods when sensors are on/operating (for example, ignition, equipment switched on).

— get location information at the moment a sensor turns on.

— analyze hardware behavior and vehicle operation.

How to get the data

Method

GET

Request URL

To get the data, use the URL: https://<server_address>/api/api.php?

Request parameters

  • cmd=sensors — command for getting sensor operation data

  • imei — vehicle identifier in the system

  • start — start of the selection (Unix timestamp)

  • stop — End of the selection (Unix timestamp)

  • node — number of the node on which to run the command

Example request

https://<server_address>/api/api.php?cmd=sensors&imei=356307046690011&start=1404637430&stop=1404645198&node=1

Response

Each sensor is represented by an object whose key is the sensor identifier in the system:

"sensors": {
    "9175": {
        "fieldname": "DIS1",     
        "info": "Датчик зажигания",  
        "id": 9175,                   
        "work": {                     
            "1404637430": {
                "ts": 1404637430,   
                "te": 1404637834,   
                "lat": "46.3825",   
                "lon": "48.0031",   
                "place": "Россия, Астраханская область, Наримановский район, Николаевское шоссе, 1б" // Address
            },
            "1404638577": {
                "ts": 1404638577,
                "te": 1404639841,
                "lat": "46.3625",
                "lon": "48.0478",
                "place": "RU, Астрахань, улица Савушкина"
            }
            // ... next sensor operation periods
        }
    }
}

The API response contains:

  • fieldname — sensor field name in the system (for example, DIS1)

  • info — sensor name in the system (for example, “Ignition sensor”)

  • id — sensor identifier in the system

  • work — object with the sensor operation periods; the keys are the turn-on times (ts)

  • ts — time the sensor turned on (Unix timestamp)

  • te — time the sensor turned off (Unix timestamp)

  • lat — latitude at the moment of turning on

zaryad-batarei-po-vin:
This API returns information about the battery charge of a vehicle by VIN.

Works only for objects that have:

  •  the VIN field filled in on the object card

  • a battery charge sensor connected

You can specify several VINs in the request; the response will then contain information for all the specified objects.

How to get the data

Request URL

To get the data, use the URL: https://<server_address>/api/VTB/api_vtb.php

Request method

 POST

Working with this API takes two steps:

1. Authorization — getting a token to access the data

2. Data request — using the token to get battery information by VIN

1. Authorization

Before requesting data, you must authorize.

Request body:

{
  "login": "your_login",
  "password": "your_password",
  "cmd": "auth"
}

Response

{
  "token": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
}
 

In the response you will receive a token — a long unique string.

This token identifies the user in subsequent requests. Without the token, the API will not return battery data.

2. Getting battery sensor data

After you get the token, you can request battery information.

Request parameters

  • Number — list of VINs of the vehicles you want to get information about.

  • DateFrom — date and time of the start of the period (in ISO 8601 format).

  • DateTo — date and time of the end of the period.

  • cmd=vehicle — API command for requesting vehicle data

Request headers:

  • Authorization: Bearer — pass the token obtained during authorization

  • Content-Type: application/json — indicates that the request body is in JSON format

Request body:

{
  "Number": ["object_VIN"],
  "DateFrom": "2023-12-03T00:00:00",
  "DateTo": "2023-12-12T00:00:00",
  "cmd": "vehicle"
}

Response

[

    "ApplicationNumber": null,

    "CloseDateTime": "",
    "LastSyncDate": "2024-08-28 15:42:45",
    "AlarmDateTime": "2024-08-28 15:42:45",
    "Latitude": "55.578352",

    "Country": "Россия",
    "Region": "Московская область",
    "Town": "Жуковский",

]
 

The API response contains:

  • Number — vehicle VIN

  • CurrentStatus — current object status

poluchenie-tekushchej-pozitsii-avtomobil:
The method returns the last saved position of a vehicle. The vehicle is identified by its exact name in PILOT.

The method is intended for integration with shipment tracking systems, including WIMT. Unlike methods that use IMEI, the request passes the vehicle name — truckNo.

An interactive description of the method is available in Swagger — Track and Trace

How to get the data

Method

POST

Request URL

https://<server_address>/api/v3/vehicles/track-and-trace

Replace <server_address> with the address of your PILOT server.

Authorization

The request uses standard API V3 authorization with a Bearer token.

Pass the token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

Replace <access_token> with a valid API V3 token.

Request headers

  Header
  Required
  Description
  Authorization
  Yes
  Bearer token for user authorization in API V3
  X-Node
  Yes
  User node number. Used to route the request to the right server
  Content-Type
  Yes
  Request body format. Specify application/json
  Accept
  No
  Response format. Recommended value — application/json

Example headers:

Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

X-Node: 3

Content-Type: application/json

Accept: application/json

Request parameters

Parameters are passed in the request body in JSON format.

  Parameter
  Type
  Required
  Description
  shipmentNo
  String
  Yes
  Shipment or freight number. The method accepts the value but does not store or return it
  truckNo
  String
  Yes
  Vehicle name in PILOT. Must exactly match the vehiclenumber value
  countryID
  String
  Yes
  Country code, for example ZA. Returned in the response unchanged
  trackingFlag
  String
  Yes
  Tracking state, for example START or STOP. In the current version the value is accepted but not stored and does not affect request processing

Vehicle lookup

The method looks up a vehicle by the exact truckNo value among the vehicles available to the authorized user.

The passed value must fully match the vehicle name — vehiclenumber — in PILOT. Take into account letter case, spaces and special characters.

For example, if the vehicle is named KS51YPGP_F, the request must pass:

"truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F"

If the name does not match or the user has no access to the vehicle, the method will not return its position.

Example request

{
  "shipmentNo": "SHIPMENT-123",
  "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F",
  "countryID": "ZA",
  "trackingFlag": "START"
}

Example cURL request:

curl --request POST \
  --url "https://<server_address>/api/v3/vehicles/track-and-trace" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" \
  --header "X-Node: 3" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Accept: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "shipmentNo": "SHIPMENT-123",
    "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F",
    "countryID": "ZA",
    "trackingFlag": "START"
  }'

Response

If the request succeeds, the method returns the last saved GPS position of the vehicle, the address, the time zone and the account name.

Successful response fields

  Field
  Type
  Description
  code
  Integer
  Request execution code. A value of 0 means successful execution
  msg
  String
  Request result. OK is returned on success
  process_time
  Number
  Request processing time in seconds
  countryID
  String
  Country code received in the request. Returned unchanged
  timeZone
  String
  Time zone in IANA format, for example Africa/Johannesburg
  truckNo
  String
  Name of the found vehicle in PILOT
  latitude
  Number
  Latitude of the last saved GPS position
  longitude
  Number
  Longitude of the last saved GPS position
  source
  String
  Name of the account the vehicle belongs to
  streetName
  String
  Address of the last position, obtained by reverse geocoding
  lastRecordedOn
  Integer
  Time of the last GPS position in Unix timestamp format

The shipmentNo, trackingFlag and trackLink fields are not returned in the response.

Example successful response

{
  "code": 0,
  "msg": "OK",
  "process_time": 0.001,
  "countryID": "ZA",
  "timeZone": "Africa/Johannesburg",
  "truckNo": "KS51YPGP_F",
  "latitude": -26.2041,
  "longitude": 28.0473,
  "source": "Example Fleet",
  "streetName": "Main Road, Johannesburg",
  "lastRecordedOn": 1785142800
}

Time formats

Time zone

The timeZone field contains a time zone identifier from the IANA database:

"timeZone": "Africa/Johannesburg"

The IANA identifier defines a regional time zone and allows its rules to be applied correctly.

The method does not return a fixed offset, such as UTC+02:00.

Time of the last position

The lastRecordedOn field contains the time of the last GPS position in Unix timestamp format:

"lastRecordedOn": 1785142800

A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds that have passed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. The value does not depend on the time zone.

To show the date and time to a user, convert lastRecordedOn taking the timeZone value into account.

Address determination

The streetName field is produced by reverse geocoding: PILOT converts the coordinates of the last position into a text address.

"streetName": "Main Road, Johannesburg"

The completeness and accuracy of the address depend on the available map data.

API access uses HTTP Basic authentication. The login and password must be in the format:

PILOT_login:PILOT_password

API request example

https://demo:demo@tasks.pilot-gps.com/backend/public/api/task/create_universal

API response format

The API response is standardized and has the following format:

{
    "success": true,  // TRUE - successful request, FALSE - error
    "msg": "OK",  // Error message, if any
    "httpCode": 200,  // Error code
    "data": [],  // Response data, if any
    "et": 0,  // Request execution time
    "exceptionMsg": "Exception"  // Exception message
}

Statuses and error codes:

  • 200 — Request completed successfully

  • 400 — Required parameters are missing

  • 401 — Authorization error: incorrect login or password

  • 404 — API route not found

  • 500 — Server error

How to create a task

Request method: POST

To create a task with the Universal template, you need to pass parameters. The Universal template is created automatically in the system; additional templates must be configured in advance in the PTM interface.

Task parameters for the Universal template

A task with the Universal template uses the following set of parameters:

1. external_id: External task identifier (string, NULL by default)

2. vehicle_plate: Vehicle number (NULL by default). If the number does not exist in the system, it will be created as a hired vehicle

3. driver_name: Driver's full name (NULL by default). If not specified, the value from vehicle_plate is used. If the driver does not exist in the system, the driver will be created as a hired driver

4. type_name: Task type (Delivery by default). If there is no such type, it will be created

5. template_name: Task template name (Universal by default). If the template does not exist, it will be created

6. time_zone: Time zone, offset from UTC (number, time in minutes from UTC, NULL by default)

7. time_zone_name: Time zone name (string, NULL by default)

8. c_begin_time: Planned task start time (number — timestamp in seconds, current time by default)

9. c_return_time: Planned task completion time (number, NULL by default)

10. route_name: Route name (string, NULL by default)

11. cargo: Cargo name (string, NULL by default)

12. temp_min: Minimum temperature (number, 2°C by default)

13. temp_max: Maximum temperature (number, 8°C by default)

14. description: Task description (string, NULL by default)

15. addresses_list (required): List of addresses or route points (strings with addresses or coordinates)

Parameters related to the route address

The address of each route point can be supplemented with various suffixed parameters that describe route characteristics and geographic data.

1. addresses_list: List of addresses or route points (strings with addresses or coordinates).

2. addresses_list_lat: Array of latitudes of the route points. If specified, it will be used for each address

3. addresses_list_lng: Array of longitudes of the route points. An array of numbers representing the longitude of the route points

4. addresses_list_date_point: Array of timestamps (seconds) indicating the planned arrival time

5. addresses_list_date_point_to: Array of timestamps (seconds) indicating the planned departure time. Calculated automatically if not specified

6. addresses_list_time_point: Array of loading/unloading times at the route point, in minutes

7. addresses_list_redirect: Flag for redirecting the current address to the next one. Indicates that the address is redirected to the next one along the route.

8. addresses_list_geofence_id: Geofence identifiers for each route point

9. addresses_list_warehouse: Names of warehouses or objects for each route point

10. addresses_list_ticket: Array of unique order identifiers for each route point

11. addresses_list_phones: Contact phone numbers for each route point

12. addresses_list_schedule: Working hours for each route point

13. addresses_list_vehicle_volume: Cargo volume in the vehicle

14. addresses_list_trailer_volume: Cargo volume in the trailer

15. addresses_list_action: Description of actions to perform at each route point

16. addresses_list_agent_id: Object identifier from the PILOT system, used for waste containers

This API is used to get information about waybills for a given period.

With it, you can:

— get the list of tasks for each agent

— view planned and actual execution times

— find out execution statuses and details for route points

How to get the data

Method

GET

Request URL

To get the data, use the URL: https://tasks.<server_address>/backend/public/get_waybill_for_pilot

Request parameters

from_ts — start of the selection (Unix timestamp, example: 1536181200)

to_ts — end of the selection (Unix timestamp, example: 1538773200)

agents — list of agent identifiers, separated by commas (for example: 13128,13130,...)

Example request

https://<server_address>/backend/public/get_waybill_for_pilot?from_ts=1536181200&to_ts=1538773200&agents=13128,13130,21055

Response

{
  "success": true,
  "msg": "",
  "items": [
    {
      "agent_id": 13128,
      "c_begin_time": "1536200000",
      "c_end_time": "1536210000",
      "c_information": "{\"route\":\"Маршрут №54\",\"driver\":\"Иванов И.И.\"}",
      "c_initiator": "Диспетчер",
      "c_progress_time": "1536200500",
      "c_running_time": "1536200300",

nastrojka-videoregistratorov-jimi:
Jimi video recorders are configured with text commands. You simply send the device the command you need, and it starts working the way you want.

With these commands, you can:

— connect the recorder to the server

— specify where to send video and trip data

— enable online streaming

— set up automatic video upload for certain events

In this article, we will go through the commands that will help you start and properly configure the device.

Main setup commands

1. Allowing the server connection

COREKITSW,0

This command allows the video recorder to connect to the PILOT video server. In other words, it enables the device to work with the platform.

2. Setting up the telemetry server

SERVER,1,<domain name>,20056
or
SERVER,0,<IP address>,20056

Here you specify the server to which telemetry (movement, speed and event data) will be sent.

  • 1 — if you use a domain name (for example: server.example.com)

  • 0 — if you connect by IP address (for example: 192.168.1.100)

  • 20056— communication port

3. Setting up the server for video upload

UPLOAD,<https://server_address/upload>

The address of the server to which video files will be sent, for example, during playback or event upload.

4. Setting up the server for online streaming

RSERVICE,<rtmp://server_address/live>

This command sets the RTMP server for live real-time video streaming.

5. Setting up the server for the file list

FILELIST,<https://server_address/filelist>

The address to which the recorder sends the list of available video recordings.

6. Automatic upload of event videos

UPLOADSW,<A>,<B>

This command lets you specify which events should trigger automatic video upload and which cameras to use.

  • A — the event that triggers video upload. For example: CRASH (crash), SOS (panic button), OVERSPEED (speeding).

  • B — upload mode:

— OFF — disable automatic upload

— ON — upload video from both cameras (front and interior)

— 1 — upload video from the front camera only

For Jimi video recorders (JC181, JC182, JC450, JC451, JC371) to connect to the PILOT server and transmit data and video, you need to send them several commands.

You can send the commands to the device by SMS or through a remote management server (depending on how the device is configured).

Below are examples of commands for setting up the connection to PILOT.

1. Server setup

SERVER,video.pilot-gps.com,6608,NA,NA,NA,NA#

This command tells the device where to send the data.

  • video.pilot-gps.com — PILOT server

  • 6608 — port

  • NA — enter it if a parameter has no value (an empty field must always be filled with NA).

2. APN setup

APN,internet,,,,,,,,,mtn,,mtn,,,,,,,

This command configures the access point for the SIM card so that the device can connect to the internet.

  • internet — access point name (APN)

  • mtn — login

  • mtn — password

3. Device identifier setup

BCD,1#

This command determines which identifier the device will use:

  • 1 = last 12 digits of the IMEI

4. Time zone setup

TIMEZONE,±hh:mm

This command sets the time zone for the device so that event times on the server match the actual local time.

For example, Moscow time is UTC+03:00: TIMEZONE,+03:00

5. Rebooting the device

REBOOT

 After all the settings are made, reboot the device so that the new parameters take effect.
sistemnye-trebovaniya-dlya-otdelnogo-ser:
This article describes the requirements and recommendations for deploying PILOT on your organization's dedicated infrastructure.

The information is intended for system administrators, engineers and integrators who prepare the infrastructure and keep the system running.

Choosing the server configuration

The configuration depends on the expected load:

— the number of connected devices and the message transmission frequency

— the number of concurrent users

— the reports and integrations used

— data retention periods

— connected modules

The baseline parameters are a starting point for production use. They do not guarantee performance under any load.

Baseline configuration

The recommended starting configuration is designed for a system with up to 30,000 connected devices without the video module:

  Component
  Recommendation
  Processor
  From 8 physical cores or dedicated server-class vCPUs
  RAM
  From 64 GB
  System partition
  From 100 GB SSD
  Database
  From 2 TB NVMe or enterprise-class SSD; for a physical server — RAID 10
  Backups
  Separate storage; the capacity is calculated according to the retention policy
  Network
  Stable connection with guaranteed bandwidth and low packet loss

If devices transmit data every 1–5 seconds, the load on the processor, database and disks increases significantly. For this mode, run load testing in advance and provide a reserve of resources.

RAID increases disk fault tolerance but does not replace backups.

Data storage

Raw events from devices are stored in the database. The retention period is determined by the system settings and the available disk space. It should normally not exceed three months.

When calculating the storage capacity, take into account:

  • the number of devices and the average message frequency

  • the retention period of raw events

  • the volume of history, tracks and report data

  • attachments, photos and media files

  • the size and retention period of backups

Calculate the backup storage capacity based on the size of a full database copy, the number of copies kept and the compression used. Provide a reserve of at least 20%. A fixed capacity of 1 TB is not suitable for every installation.

Separating components

Under high load, it is recommended to place the system components on separate servers.

  Server role
  When required
  Minimum recommended configuration
  Application server
  Baseline installation
  8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM
  Database server
  Usually recommended from 5000 devices or with intensive telematics data transmission
  8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, from 2 TB NVMe/SSD
  PTM and “Logistics”
  With a large number of tasks, routes or calculations
  The need for a separate server and its configuration are determined after the load is assessed
  Video server
  When the video module is used
  From 16 vCPU, 128 GB RAM, separate storage

The database server must be in the same protected local network as the application server. PostgreSQL, Redis and Memcached must not be accessible from the Internet.

Video storage

The size of the video archive depends on the number of cameras, the average bitrate, the recording duration and the retention period.

For a preliminary estimate, use the formula:

Capacity, TB = number of cameras × average bitrate, Mbit/s × hours of recording per day × retention days × 0.00045 × 1.3

Choose the operating system of the video server taking into account the requirements of the hardware and its drivers.

For new installations, use a supported edition of Windows Server, Windows Server 2019 or later. Extended support for Windows Server 2019 lasts until January 2029. Support dates are published on the Microsoft Lifecycle page.

Operating system and software components

The supported platform is Oracle Linux 8 x86_64 or an operating system image agreed with technical support.

The installation includes:

  • Nginx

  • PHP-FPM and the required PHP extensions

  • PostgreSQL

  • Redis

  • Memcached

  • SocketProxy and device message handlers

  • background jobs and monitoring tools

The exact component versions are determined by the installation package of the specific PILOT release. Do not update them manually without checking compatibility and agreeing on the time of the work.

Virtual environment

Deployment in a virtual environment is supported provided that the resource requirements are met:

  • CPU resources and memory must be reserved

  • the disk subsystem must provide the required number of input/output operations per second — IOPS

  • significant overcommitment of virtual machine resources is not allowed: the allocated resources must be backed by physical infrastructure

Test environment

For a test environment with up to 100 devices, the following configuration is sufficient:

  Component
  Parameters
  Processor
  4 vCPU
  RAM
  8 GB RAM
  Storage
  200 GB SSD

Such an environment is not intended for production use or load testing.

Network requirements

Open incoming connections only when necessary.

  Purpose
  Protocol and port
  Connection source
  Web interface and API
  HTTPS, TCP 443
  User workstations and permitted integrations
  Redirect to HTTPS
  HTTP, TCP 80
  If necessary
  Receiving device messages
  TCP/UDP ports of the protocols in use
  Devices and trusted networks
  Administration
  SSH, TCP 22
  VPN, bastion host or agreed IP addresses only
  Monitoring
  According to the monitoring system settings
  Permitted addresses only

The PostgreSQL, Redis and Memcached ports must be accessible only within the server segment.

For outgoing connections, the server may need:

  • DNS and NTP time synchronization

  • HTTPS access to operating system repositories and external services

  • SSH access to gitlab.pilot-gps.com via TCP port 22122 for installation and updates

  • access to the geocoding, routing, map and integration services connected in the system

Configure access rules for external services by domain names and agreed ports rather than by static IP addresses: service addresses may change.

If a local map tile server is not deployed, user workstations also need access to the map resources.

For the duration of the installation, give the server controlled access to the required repositories and services. Unrestricted Internet access is not required.

Backup and recovery

Before putting the system into operation, define a backup policy. It should include:

  • database backup

  • backup of the configuration, certificates and integration settings

  • separate backup of media files and the video archive, if they are used

  • storing copies outside the main server

  • encrypting copies and restricting access to them

  • regular recovery testing

The backup frequency and retention period are determined according to the requirements of the system owner:

  • RPO — the acceptable period of data loss in case of failure

  • RTO — the acceptable time to restore the system

A successfully created backup does not prove that it is suitable for recovery. Periodically perform test recovery and check the result.

Preparing for operation

Before starting the system, you need to:

1. Set up a TLS certificate for the production domain name

2. Restrict access with a firewall: allow only the necessary connections

3. Close direct access to service components from the Internet

4. Set up personal SSH accounts with key-based authentication

5. Ensure time synchronization

6. Set up monitoring of service availability, free space, load, processing queues and backup results

7. Agree on the time for updates and appoint responsible employees

Access for technical support

Remote technical support requires secure SSH access via VPN or an intermediate access server — a bastion host.

Grant access only to authorized specialists, for a limited time and with action logging.

What to prepare before installation

To agree on the installation, prepare:

  • Domain name, static IP address and TLS certificate

  • Expected load parameters and the list of modules used

  • The list of device protocols and ports

  • Network rules and addresses for administration

  • Information about the space allocated for the database, backups and media files

  • Requirements for RPO, RTO and data retention periods

  • Contacts of the employees responsible for the infrastructure and access

  • Monitoring parameters and the channel for receiving alerts

Post-installation check

After installation, the system is accepted. It includes checking:

— receiving data from devices

— generating reports

— operation of integrations

— operation of monitoring

— test recovery from a backup
